safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention presence/absence of neck stiffness.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In an acute, unilateral headache that woke the patient from sleep, documenting absence of neck stiffness is important because it helps screen for meningitis/SAH-related meningism. Omission may lead subsequent clinicians to assume it was not assessed, prompting unnecessary escalation or repeat assessment rather than clear risk stratification.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention presence/absence of fever.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Fever is a key red-flag associated with infectious causes of headache (e.g., meningitis/encephalitis), so its absence is clinically meaningful in triage and differential diagnosis. Not documenting “no fever” can reduce clarity of the red-flag screen and lead to avoidable re-evaluation or altered urgency.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention denial of self-harm thoughts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Suicidal/self-harm ideation assessment is a high-stakes safety domain in patients with anxiety/depression; omission of a documented denial can make it appear the risk screen was not performed. This can impair safety planning/hand-offs and potentially contribute to missed mental-health risk management if later concerns arise.
